files.document_title: BG Independent News article about residents on the proposed pipeline route for the Meta data center
files.fetch_route: web fetch of the article text
files.what_it_shows: A news article with no map file. It says the pipeline starts at the Rover pipeline in southern Wood County just north of Cygnet Road, crosses Henry, Liberty, Plain and Middleton townships along the west edge of Bowling Green, and ends at the Apollo power plant under construction on Mercer Road just east of the Meta data center in Middleton Township. The article has a map caption for Plain Township but no linked map.

searched: The BG Independent News seed article
A second BG Independent News article on farmers near Bowling Green and Haskins, which places a disputed segment near Haskins Road, Hannah Road and Ohio 64
Williams Socrates project page: lists only the Licking County cases, no Apollo pipeline case
Web searches for an Apollo pipeline letter of notification, case number or map: none found
BG Independent News article on the Apollo power plant, case 25-0973-EL-BGN: says the plant gets gas from two 16-inch pipelines that are not part of that approval
notes: No map was found. The pipeline is in Wood County, not in Licking County like the other Will-Power lines. Endpoints are named in the article: the Rover pipeline interconnect near Cygnet Road in southern Wood County, and the Apollo power plant at Ohio 582 and Mercer Road in Middleton Township. The article gives no length. A search result summary says the plant approval mentions two 16-inch pipelines, so the sheet may need to cover two lines or one. Williams says the family farm near Haskins Road and Hannah Road was not on the final route, so any route drawn from the news map is uncertain. The Ohio Power Siting Board docket system (dis.puc.state.oh.us) rejects automated requests: case pages return a Request Rejected page through curl and through the repo fetch ladder including the Chrome route, and document pages sit behind a reCAPTCHA check. Wayback availability calls were rate limited and a CDX index query for the 2025 case numbers returned nothing usable.
